Question: How can you make money while programming?
Answer: Usually at the end of each month, a company puts large sums of money into my bank account and call it salary. I like this system. Question: What is organic food, and how is it different from any other?
Answer: Here is the marketing Imagine a farmer from the 1940s or even 1880s. Modern equipment at the time, rich harvest, healthy kids, healthy family. Good times. Hell no, it was the best of times. Except, reality wasn’t told about this story, not anymore than the imaginary 1950–1960s, the image people look back at (white upper middle class people), simply did not exist. The only thing that was true, people who look back and think this was great, were kids at that time. Anyway. What marketing omits to say and talk about is how back breaking this was. How farmers borrowed money to plant seeds and hopefully could pay back in the fall. But lack of rain, too much rain, crop failures, locusts, rats, rodents happened. back then you had to rest parts of your land. People got sick from poo infested crops. Children did not reach 10 years of age was the norm, most of your kids died was the norm. Children once they could walk, worked. Hard labor. It wasn’t the good old days. It was reality. Reality. There will not be any produce on these lands this summer because the winter was longer than usual. Today, we have crops that need less pesticides, less water and thrive in places it would normally not grow just 50 some years ago. Organic food is just marketing scam. It claims to be organic and therefore all other food is not organic, somehow. All food is organic. The Organic marketing is just that, marketing. They market products that are worse, smaller yields, less nutrients, smaller produce, less vitamins and they require a lot more water and pesticides which includes even copper, which is something you should not eat. It takes more time to grow and is much more expensive. And this isn’t to help your farmer in anyway. The same companies own both food products. Yes, Kellogg's, Nestlé, Kraft and the rest. If people will pay more for worse products, think they will not be there? It is just a scam. The idea is lofty, lovely even but it is like Disney with it’s talking animals. Reality simply is saying other things. I simply have one rule when it comes to shopping. I don’t buy products that say Organic on them. If they ever are in my house, it was by accident or because it was the only available product and I badly needed it.
